title: Reconcile Two Service Responses
statement: Two JSON objects arrive describing the same customer from different backend services: `profile` (first line) and `contacts` (second line). Merge `contacts` into `profile` using these rules: (1) start with every field from `profile`; (2) for each field in `contacts` that doesn't exist yet in the merged record, add it as-is; (3) if a field is a list in both records, merge them by concatenating profile's list then any new contacts items not already present, preserving order (no duplicates); (4) otherwise, if the contacts value is not null, it overwrites the existing value; if it IS null, keep the existing profile value. Print the merged JSON object with keys sorted alphabetically and compact separators, e.g. json.dumps(merged, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).
starter_code:
import json

profile = json.loads(input())
contacts = json.loads(input())

# TODO: merge `contacts` into `profile` following the rules above, then
# print json.dumps(merged, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).
hints: Start with merged = dict(profile), then loop over contacts.items()
Use isinstance(value, list) checks on both sides before deciding to concatenate instead of overwrite
A None value in contacts means 'no update' - keep whatever profile already had for that key
